static_traits.name: Lin Lu
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet received treatment for psychological problems; has not yet experienced similar problems; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: First consultation, feeling nervous but with a positive attitude; clear expression, capable of self-reflection; good cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: I struggle with making decisions, especially simple things like choosing between a spicy corn dog and a cheese corn dog. My indecisiveness makes me believe I am bad at decision-making, affecting my confidence and self-esteem.
basic_info.core_demands: Because long-term decision difficulty affects daily life and relationships, hopes to obtain guidance and support and improve decision-making ability.

core_beliefs: I am a person who is terrible at making decisions
If I make the wrong choice it will bring negative consequences and others will judge me

special_situations.event: At a restaurant dining with family, needs to choose between a spicy corn hot dog and a cheese hot dog
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I choose wrong, I will ruin this meal and disappoint my family
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly weighs options and delays decisions, seeking advice from family to reduce the probability of errors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I choose wrong, this meal will be ruined by me and everyone will not be happy

special_situations.event: Partner feels depressed about my indecisiveness and expresses dissatisfaction with me
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot make quick and correct decisions, it means I am immature and terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding making decisions or letting others decide, to reduce the risk of being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He must think I am terrible and cannot make decisions

special_situations.event: In daily life, when asked for an opinion or when a choice needs to be made (such as arranging activities, deciding what meal to make)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If an option is not perfect, it is wrong; I must make the right choice
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Making pros-and-cons lists, constantly comparing, trying to find the 'only correct' answer
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Either choose right or choose wrong; I cannot make mistakes

special_situations.event: Recalling past experiences of indecision and facing new choice situations
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I have often made poor decisions in the past, so it will be the same later
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Preemptively avoids choice situations; reduces the number of times facing decisions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I always make poor decisions; this time will be no exception

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted, and to be seen as someone who can make 'good decisions'
core_conflict.fear: Fearing making the wrong choice and being judged, disappointing others, and damaging relationships
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being evaluated and making mistakes by avoiding and delaying decisions and letting others decide

object_relations.self_representation: An indecisive self, prone to mistakes and subject to judgment
object_relations.object_representation: The other party (partner / family) is a critical observer who is easily disappointed

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked by others (including the counselor or family) to give a clear choice or opinion
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other person is judging whether I make the 'right' decision; if not perfect they will negate me
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Listing pros and cons in an analytical tone, constantly comparing details, prolonging the decision process; trying not to touch on feelings and uncertainty.

manifestations: When facing choices, experiences high pressure and a sense of responsibility, worrying that wrong choices will bring consequences and others' judgment
Treats everyday small decisions as high-risk events and pursues the 'perfect choice'

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequently self-blaming and applying negative labels to myself ('I am terrible')
Overly concerned with possible judgment from others and reduces spontaneous expression

contact_model.definition: Taking external rules and expectations as one's own standards or absolute truth without digesting them.
manifestations: Judges daily decisions by the standard of 'must make the correct/perfect choice'
Uses others' possible evaluations as the measure of self-worth

exception_events.target_problem: When planning family activities, the client usually hesitates, procrastinates, and worries about choosing wrong, leading to increased stress and tension with her partner.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Unique outcome: once when deciding to take the family to the park, she did not overthink details as usual, but focused on everyone's enjoyment; the whole family had a wonderful time, and she felt relieved with boosted confidence.
exception_events.reason: Clue: different understanding - shifting focus from 'perfect choice' to 'overall experience and others' enjoyment'; different approach - deciding faster with less repeated comparison.

positive_force: Has a supportive partner and adult children to communicate with
Having had successful experience organizing family activities, able to shift focus to the experience
Positive attitude, willing to try and practice decision-making
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking dominate the decision process
Mind reading and personalization cause excessive concern about others' judgments
Over-relies on pros-and-cons lists and others' opinions, forming a pattern of avoidance and procrastination
Impaired self-esteem, negative self-labels ('I am terrible')

target_behavior.behavior: Indecisiveness and avoidance/procrastination when facing choices, with marked anxiety
antecedent: Restaurant ordering situations (choosing between two dishes)
Being asked for an opinion by partner or family
Choices requiring arranging family activities or daily tasks
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and perfectionistic cognition about 'choosing wrong will bring negative consequences and be judged', accompanied by excessive attention to others' possible opinions
target_behavior.function: Escaping the potential risks of being judged and making mistakes, briefly relieving anxiety and uncertainty.
target_behavior.consequence: Affecting daily tasks and arrangements, creating tension with her partner; confidence and decreased self-esteem.
